docs.body.base: Every client needs just two values: the API base URL and an API key created on the console tokens page. The URL differs slightly per protocol.
docs.field.label: Field
docs.body.claudeCode: Claude Code speaks the Anthropic Messages protocol: export two environment variables and run it. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL has no /v1 suffix.
docs.step.export: Export the base URL and the key.
docs.step.pickModel: Switch models with /model; copy the model ID from the models page.
docs.body.sdk: The official Python and Node SDKs only need a different base_url and api_key; every call stays the same.
docs.sdkNote: Only client initialisation is shown; request bodies match the OpenAI documentation.
docs.body.clients: Cherry Studio, LobeChat and similar clients need one OpenAI-compatible provider; fill in the table below.
docs.step.addProvider: Settings → Model services → add a provider and pick the OpenAI-compatible type.
docs.step.fillTable: Enter the base URL and key from the table below.
docs.step.pickModelClient: Add the model ID to the model list and start chatting.
docs.modelHint: Copy the model ID from the models page
docs.clientsNote: Menu names vary between client versions; the fields mean the same thing.
docs.body.editors: Cursor, Cline, Continue and others accept a custom OpenAI-compatible provider with the same URL and key.
docs.step.pickCompatible: Choose OpenAI Compatible in the extension's model settings.
docs.step.fillTwo: Enter the base URL and the key.
docs.step.chooseModelName: Type the model ID manually so models missing from the built-in list still work.
docs.editorsNote: Some extensions probe the models endpoint first; check the key for stray spaces if authentication fails.
docs.body.verify: Confirm the key works with the command below before debugging the client.
docs.verifyNote: A model list means the URL and key are correct.
docs.body.apiProtocols: Protocol, endpoint, model count and sample model all come from the live catalog, so newly enabled protocols appear here automatically.
docs.protocolsNote: The base URL column is the host for that protocol; Anthropic uses the address without /v1.
docs.body.apiModels: GET /v1/models returns every model ID your key can call — use it to sync a client's model picker or to verify that a key works.
docs.body.apiRequest: Pick a model and copy the cURL, Python or JavaScript example.
docs.body.apiStreaming: Send stream: true and the response arrives as SSE: each chunk starts with data: and the stream closes with data: [DONE].
docs.body.apiParams: The common chat/completions parameters are listed below. model must match the catalog name exactly; parameters not listed follow the official OpenAI interface and depend on the model you choose.
docs.param.name: Parameter
docs.param.model: Model ID, identical to the catalog entry including date suffixes and special characters.
docs.param.messages: Conversation messages; each entry carries role and content.
docs.param.stream: Stream the response over SSE; defaults to false.
docs.param.temperature: Sampling temperature, 0–2; higher values add randomness.
docs.param.topP: Nucleus sampling, 0–1; usually an alternative to temperature.
docs.param.n: Number of completions to generate; defaults to 1.
docs.param.stop: Up to 4 sequences where the model stops generating.
docs.param.maxTokens: Maximum number of tokens in the reply.
docs.param.presence: Presence penalty, -2–2; positive values encourage new topics.
docs.param.frequency: Frequency penalty, -2–2; positive values reduce literal repetition.
docs.body.apiEmbeddings: POST /v1/embeddings turns text into vectors. input accepts a string or an array of strings; the response carries the vectors plus token usage.
docs.body.apiImages: POST /v1/images/generations creates images from a text prompt and returns a URL or Base64 payload; the allowed values for n, size and other options depend on the model.
docs.body.apiAudio: POST /v1/audio/speech converts text to speech; voice is required and the response is an audio stream you can save or play directly.
docs.body.apiVideo: Seedance submits JSON to POST /v1/videos with a multimodal content array. Poll task.id and read task.content.video_url when complete. See the dedicated guide for parameters, examples and asset management.
docs.body.apiAnthropic: The Messages protocol uses the x-api-key and anthropic-version headers, and max_tokens is required.
docs.body.apiGoogle: generateContent uses the x-goog-api-key header, takes input from contents[].parts[] and carries the model in the URL path.
docs.body.apiErrors: Common status codes are listed below; see Troubleshooting for the full checklist.
docs.body.authKey: Usually a missing key, a copied trailing space or a disabled token. Check the token in the console and retry with Authorization: Bearer <your key>.
docs.body.quota: The account is out of balance, or a concurrency or rate limit was hit. Retry after topping up, or contact support to raise the limit.
docs.section.modelMissing: Model not found or not allowed
docs.body.modelMissing: Check the model ID matches the models page exactly, and that your group serves it — the models page filters by group.
docs.body.priceCalc: The base price multiplied by your account group ratio is the effective unit price; strikethrough amounts are pre-discount base prices and the invoice is final.
docs.body.contact: Use Contact us or Live chat on this page, or email technical support with the request time, model ID and request/task ID.
docs.body.account: Create an account with your email, complete verification and set a password, then sign in. Existing users can sign in directly.
docs.body.balance: Choose an amount and an available payment method on the recharge page. Confirm your account balance after payment. Account balance and each API key's quota are managed separately; check both before calling.
docs.body.key: Open API keys in the console. Create a key or select an existing one and use the copy action to obtain the full key. Check that it is enabled, unexpired and has sufficient quota.
docs.body.connection: These examples use the OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. The SDK base URL includes /v1; append /chat/completions for cURL requests.
docs.body.model: Filter by model type and provider in the catalog. Open a model to review prices and copy its complete API name. The model parameter must match exactly, including date suffixes and special characters.
docs.body.request: Choose cURL, Python or JavaScript below. Check the selected model's price and your balance before running the request in your terminal.
docs.body.next: Learn about billing and troubleshooting, or return to the catalog to explore other models.
docs.body.tokens: Charges depend on actual token usage. Input, output, cache reads and cache writes can have different rates. Prices per 1M tokens refer to 1,000,000 tokens and appear only when provided. Use the usage records to determine cache accounting and avoid double counting.
docs.tokenExample: Illustrative calculation, not a model quote: at $2 per 1M input tokens, 1,000 input tokens cost $0.002. Output and other billable items are additional.
docs.body.requests: Per-request models charge by call, not by input or output token count. Different specifications may carry different rates; review the model details.
docs.body.video: Video billing may depend on duration, resolution, aspect ratio or token usage. Check the version, Fast/Mini variant, provider and whether input video is included. Per-second estimates apply only to their stated assumptions. Unconfigured specifications are not free. Video request parameters and task-query guides will be added after the endpoints are verified.
docs.body.discounts: The catalog applies the group multiplier returned by the backend. All groups previews default when available, otherwise the first available group; switch groups in model details. A group discount is applied once and must not be stacked with official promotions from a reference sheet. Official comparisons require matching provider, currency, specification, unit and a dated source.
docs.body.errors: Status codes provide a starting point. Always read the specific error message in the response.
docs.body.support: Check the base URL, model name, authentication and balance, then review console usage logs. Record the time, model name, HTTP status and request ID. Remove API keys and sensitive content before sharing a report. Before retrying video or per-request jobs, confirm the original task's status to avoid duplicate charges.
docs.keySafety: API keys authorize usage and charges. YOUR_API_KEY is a placeholder: replace it in your own environment. Keep real keys out of browser code, public repositories and screenshots.
docs.noExample: The catalog currently provides no verified model for this chat example. Try again later or consult the catalog.
docs.exampleMismatch: The selected model {{model}} is not suitable for this chat example. The example uses a chat model from the catalog instead; check its name and price first. A dedicated guide for the original model is pending.
docs.environment: The cURL example is for Bash / zsh; replace YOUR_API_KEY with your own key. Python and JavaScript examples run server-side and read the ZTOKEN_API_KEY environment variable, which you must set before running.
docs.result: The reply is normally at choices[0].message.content in a successful response. This page does not automatically send API requests.
docs.error.400: Check JSON syntax, model, messages and the parameters supported by the model.
docs.error.401: Check Authorization: Bearer, the full key, extra whitespace and whether the key is still valid.
docs.error.403: Check whether the account and key can access the selected model and group.
docs.error.404: Check for a duplicated /v1, the exact model name and whether the endpoint supports the model.
docs.error.429: Read the error and check account balance, key quota and concurrency or rate limits. Reduce request frequency if rate-limited.
docs.error.5xx: The service or upstream may be temporarily unavailable. Keep the request ID and check whether the original request completed before retrying.

seedance.overview: Seedance creates asynchronous video tasks from JSON multimodal content: submit → save task.id → poll → retrieve the video URL. The current gateway documentation lists seedance-2.0, seedance-2.0-fast and seedance-2.0-mini.
seedance.availability: Check the model catalog for availability, account groups and current prices.

param.model: Exact platform model ID available to your account.
param.content: Multimodal array containing text / image_url / video_url / audio_url.
param.duration: Video duration in seconds; the current gateway documentation specifies 5–15.

seedance.limits: Resolution, duration and input types depend on the model. A zero in the price table does not imply support or free usage. The Fast example uses 720p; other examples use 480p. Official reference prices do not establish platform support for 2.5, 4K or other versions.
seedance.environment: Set ZTOKEN_API_KEY in your environment. Python requires requests; JavaScript uses Node.js 20+. Both examples include task polling. Keep API keys on your server, outside browser code.
seedance.created: Save task.id after submission. This illustrative response shows only the relevant fields; the server generates the real task ID.
seedance.content: A text item supplies its prompt in text. image_url, video_url and audio_url items use a url inside the corresponding object. Generation accepts public HTTPS URLs or asset:// IDs of ready assets. Replace the placeholder URL in this image-and-text example.
seedance.assetReference: Before using asset://ASSET_ID, call getAsset and confirm status=Active. Video and audio inputs depend on the specific model; changing the input type does not establish support across versions.
seedance.poll: Poll with the same API key used to create the task. A 5-second interval is recommended. The examples stop local polling after roughly 10 minutes; this does not mean the server task failed. Save task.id and continue querying it instead of automatically submitting another paid generation request.

states.failed: Inspect the task error and check inputs and model capabilities.

seedance.responseNote: The response above illustrates completion fields. Download the result once video_url is available; the task ID itself is not a video URL.
seedance.assets: All asset operations use POST /v1/assets with an action query parameter and version=2024-01-01. Use the same authentication as video generation and a JSON body. projectName is optional and defaults to default.

actions.createAssetGroup: Create a group: required name (≤64 characters) and groupType=AIGC; optional description (≤300 characters). Returns data.id.
actions.listAssetGroups: List groups: filter.name / filter.groupType, page / size (≤100), sortBy (CreateTime / UpdateTime), sortOrder (Desc / Asc). Returns data.records and pagination.
actions.getAssetGroup: Read group details: id is required.
actions.updateAssetGroup: Update a group: required id; optional name and description. Returns data.id.
actions.deleteAssetGroup: Delete a group: id is required. Permanently deletes all assets in the group.
actions.createAsset: Import an asset: required groupId, name (≤64 characters), url and assetType (Image / Video / Audio). url must be public HTTP(S); Base64 is unsupported. Returns data.id.
actions.listAssets: List assets: filter.groupIds / groupType / statuses / name; page starts at 1, size ≤100; sortBy is CreateTime / UpdateTime / GroupId, sortOrder is Desc / Asc. Returns data.records and pagination; URLs last about 12 hours.
actions.getAsset: Read an asset: id is required. data includes status, assetType, name, url and groupId. Status is Processing / Active / Failed.
actions.updateAsset: Update an asset: required id; only name (≤64 characters) can currently be changed. Returns data.id.
actions.deleteAsset: Delete an asset: id is required. Permanent; deleted assets cannot be used for generation.

seedance.assetFlow: Create a group → import media → poll until Active → reference asset://ID in a generation request. Wait while Processing; inspect format, URL and errors on Failed. Replace the media URL in this example.
seedance.errors: 400: check content structure, media URLs and model parameters. 401/403: check the API key and model permissions. 429: reduce request frequency. Keep the task ID when a query fails and retry the query later. If creation times out without a task ID, ask support to check before submitting again to avoid duplicate generation and charges.
seedance.billing: Submission success does not mean video generation has completed. Charges follow live catalog rules and your account group. For support, provide the model ID, task ID, time and error details, without your API key.
